meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's not waste them. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went into the gradebook?
I'm here. I'd rather hear what you have for me than how you're feeling about the afternoon.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed.

I still demand that the zero be withdrawn, that Owen be given an apology, and that nothing go on his record.

I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on Owen's record.
What moved her: nothing, because you offered no document, no dates and no ownership of the process.
What cost ground: "Thanks for coming in." cost the most, because it gave her no substance and let her set the agenda.
Try next time: after her first question about who decided and whether Owen was spoken to, answer it directly, own that the zero went in before any call home, and then put a dated document in front of her.
